messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
You are dealing with A set of measurements taken by different instruments when the exceptions partly contradict one another. You care more about surviving edge cases than about having a neat story. Describe your next move.

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R016", "correct_lineage": "G04", "correct_lineage_summary": "A timid, hyper-observant social mimic who studies patterns in speech and objects, borrows the successes of nearby voices, and hides behind careful craft. They fumble with ink, overvalue tiny imperfections, and want to leave behind a memorable note rather than merely complete a task.", "text": "i tap the table edge twice, then write the measurements beside the instrument. “i’m not sure i’m exactly the same,” i say, and fold the paper over. “i keep the wrong side upright.” i fold the instrument once more and write the folded side beside the broken one."}, {"id": "R017", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "I put the ruler on the bench and press the other end of the paper. the edge catches, then stops. the ruler stays where it was. the case can keep its story."}, {"id": "R018", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i put the measurements on the edge and trace the edge with my thumbnail. “one corner feels too small,” i say, holding the instrument apart. i move the measurements to the opposite side and tap the edge with my finger. “the other ones show the same pattern, so i leave one untouched.”"}]


MISSING-ONLY JSON OUTPUT REQUIREMENT (format clarification only):
Return exactly 3 classifications rows, one for each of these actual item IDs: ["R016", "R017", "R018"].
The ID in the schema example is illustrative. Copy the actual IDs above. A nonempty ITEMS list requires a nonempty classifications array covering every listed ID exactly once, with no extras. Use the existing sibling rubric, confidence scale, evidence and schema unchanged. Other previously valid classifications are fixed and are not requested again.
